The Lord Jesus Christ invites the daughters of the human race to be his bride. He greatly desires their beauty. He means those who forget their own people and their father’s house, who listen, think it over, and lean toward his invitation, and who join themselves to him in this relationship.
I will show you these things:
I. How Christ joins himself in marriage to people, and especially to women.

The Lord Jesus Christ joins himself in marriage to people here in this world. But the public wedding ceremony will wait until the last day. On that day his bride will be brought to him in white robes, dressed in perfect righteousness. My dear sisters, that clothing will be richer and finer than any of your needlework. The wedding feast will be held in his Father’s house in heaven. Then his people will be welcomed into the closest, warmest embrace of his love.
The marriage knot is tied here on earth, and it includes four things:
First, both choose each other.
Second, both love each other.
Third, both are joined together.
Fourth, both are bound by promises to each other.

First, my dear sisters, both choose each other. This choosing happens in Christ as the Mediator. But it is also done by Christ as the eternal Son of God, yes, as God himself. That is true, no matter what the polished Arians and Socinians say against it.

My dear sisters, the Lord Jesus Christ chooses you only because of his free grace. He brings you into the marriage promise freely, out of his own mercy. You have offended him so badly, and yet the Lord Jesus Christ has chosen you. You did not choose him, and you would not have chosen him. But once he has chosen you, my dear sisters, then—and only then—you choose him as your Lord and Husband.

When the Lord Jesus Christ first comes to you, he finds you full of sin and filth. Because of sin, you are ugly, stained, enslaved, poor, miserable, and wretched. You are low and disgusting. He does not choose you because you are holy, or beautiful, or good enough for these things. No, the Lord Jesus Christ puts those good qualities on you, so that you are fit for his embrace. And you are drawn to choose the Lord Jesus Christ because he chose you first.
Second, my dear sisters, in this marriage of yours both love each other. This love goes along with the choosing.

Your hearts reach out for Christ. Your souls pant and long for him. You cannot rest until you are promised to this Jesus. You feel like crying out all the time, “Only Christ! Only Christ!” This is what your hearts say, if you truly feel how much you need him.
The better you get to know this Lord Jesus, the happier you are with your choice, and the more your love is drawn to him.
And where could you put your love better than on Jesus, who poured out his blood for you?
He surely deserves all your love and affection. Keep going, keep going, my dear sisters, so that your love grows stronger and stronger.

Third, there is not only choosing each other and loving each other, but also being joined together. This joining is the main thing in the marriage. Christ and souls are joined by promise, and the knot is tied so tight that no one can undo it. Not people on earth, however powerful they are. Not devils in hell, even if they put all their anger and rage together. They cannot break it. They cannot untie it. No, my dear sisters, it can never be undone. On Christ’s side, the joining is by the Spirit. On your side, it is by faith. By the Spirit, Christ takes hold of you. By faith, you take hold of him. That is how the match is made. Christ becomes yours: his person, his inheritance, and all his gifts are yours. And you become Christ’s: your selves, your hearts, and everything you have are handed over to him. Oh, may that be true more and more!
Fourth, Christ and his bride are bound by promises to each other.

Christ promises to love you here. He will not leave you. No, he will never leave you. He will protect you from the hatred of the Pharisees of our day. He will take care of you in every hard time. He will live with you here. And at last he will take you to himself, to live with him forever.

And you promise to be loving, loyal, faithful, and obedient to him. You are to stay close to him as long as you live. Then you will find that you have made the best marriage there is, for your soul and your body, for this life and for eternity.
II. Christ invites all of you to be his bride.
That is why he sends out his ministers to preach.
That is why I have come among you like this. I want you to accept this invitation. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I call you, and I beg you, to take him on his own terms.

He calls all of you, my sisters, who are willing to be married to the Lord Jesus Christ. Old or young, married or single, high or low—even the poorest servants. Yes, he calls you even if the world calls you “the rabble of this world.”
I tell you, the poor are just as welcome to be Christ’s bride as the rich.

He does not care more about the rich than the poor. He chose a humble young woman, engaged to a carpenter, to be his mother. And he chooses and calls people like that to be his bride. So do not be discouraged when the world looks down on you. If Christ loves you and you are married to him, that will be more than enough to make up for all the trouble you have faced here.
III. Those who want to be married to Christ must listen, think carefully, and lean toward his invitation. They must even forget their father’s house.
Those who want to be married to Christ must listen.

“Listen, O daughter.” My sisters, many of you block your ears against the calls of the gospel. You close your ears like the deaf snake that will not listen to the snake charmer, no matter how skillfully he charms.
You will not listen to Christ’s invitations. You can listen to the empty things of the world, and enjoy the world’s marriages. But you never think about Christ’s marriage, and you never enjoy it.

Sin’s temptation came in through the ear to the first man, when he turned away from God. In the same way, the invitation to be Christ’s bride must come in through the ear. Only then will the heart open to receive Jesus Christ in this marriage.
My dear sisters, if you want to be married to Christ, you must think carefully about his invitation.

Just hearing Christ’s invitation quickly or casually will not help you. It will not make the match between Christ and your souls. No, you must receive Christ in your heart. You must think about the marriage itself and its benefits. You must think about how Christ’s invitations are different from the devil’s temptations, or from anything the world offers you.
Those who want to be married to Christ must be willing to accept his invitation.
“Listen, O daughter, think it over, and bend your ear.”

This means bending your hearts. You must agree with your will. You must go along with what Christ is asking. You must long for Christ. Then your hearts will say, “Lord, let us be your bride, and you be the one we love.”
You must also forget your father’s house.
“Listen, O daughter, think it over, and forget your father’s house.”

This does not mean you must stop loving your family. But you must forget all your relatives in this way: you must be ready to give up their approval whenever it competes with the approval of the Lord Jesus Christ. And do not let your worldly friends and relatives stop you from coming to the Lord Jesus and marrying him.

I beg you with all my heart: be willing to lose anything rather than lose his favor. You must truly forget your own people. That means you must forget all the bad habits you learned in your father’s house. You must give up your empty way of living—reading plays, novels, and romances. And you must stay away from learning the songs that drunkards sing. For if you are Christ’s bride, he has bought you back.
My dear sisters, those of you who are married to the Lord Jesus Christ are very beautiful.

I do not mean your bodies. You may be less good-looking on the outside than others. But your souls will be more beautiful than anyone’s—not so much in people’s eyes as in God’s eyes. People like this have the beautiful image of God stamped on them. No one else in the world has even the smallest spark of spiritual beauty.
Those who are not married to Christ have not been made new. They are not born again. They have not been brought from sin to God. And that has to happen before you can be married to Christ.

The Lord Jesus Christ wants to see this beauty in his bride. He cries out, “My dove, you are hiding in the cracks of the rock, in the secret places of the stairway. Show me your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet, and your face is beautiful.”

He calls his bride “my love,” because she is the one he dearly loves. He admires how lovely she is. He even says it twice in one verse: “Look how beautiful you are, my love! Look how beautiful you are!”
So you see how he describes their beauty.
And then, my sisters, Christ says something wonderful to his bride: “You have won my heart, my sister, my bride. You have won my heart with just one of your eyes, with one chain around your neck.”
So you see how pleased the Lord Jesus Christ is with his bride. So won’t you marry the Lord Jesus?
I offer Jesus Christ to all of you. Maybe you have been famous for your sins. Maybe you have been as great a prostitute as Mary Magdalene was. Once you are married to Christ, you will be forgiven.

So do not be discouraged by the insults and scorn the world may throw at you. Come and join yourselves to the Lord Jesus Christ, and all your sins will be washed away in his blood. Once you are married to Jesus, you are separated from sin. You are born again.

Right now it is as if you are married to sin. Sin is your husband, and you like it too much. But once you are married to Christ, when you are born again, then you can be said to die to sin. Until then, sin lives in the things you love. So, my sisters, give sin its deadly wound in your hearts. God’s word has called you again and again, and it has made no difference to you. But when you are married to the Lord Jesus Christ, his Spirit will bring you to him. Then you will take hold of him by faith. His Spirit will draw you to himself. He will make you willing in the day of his power. He will give you faith in him.

Faith is the hand of the soul that takes hold of Christ. So do not be satisfied until this gift of faith has been powerfully worked in you. Do not be satisfied until you have received the Lord Jesus Christ.

Hold Christ in the arms of your deepest love. You truly love the Lord Jesus Christ when you love him and value him more than your father, your mother, and all the joys and pleasures of this life. But if you enjoy anything this world can give more than the Lord Jesus Christ, you do not truly love him.

If you are married to Christ, you know him and talk with him. You will try to help his cause and make his name known in the world. When others go off to the fancy, fashionable entertainments of life, you will be working to bring honor to the Lord Jesus Christ. You will praise the one you love above every other loved one. And you will try to bring others to love him too.
My dear sisters, you have come together now to worship God. Can you show proof like this that you are married to the Lord Jesus Christ?
Oh, how joyful and comforting it is to be in this state!
Surely this marriage is worth looking for. It is the only marriage truly worth wanting. And the Lord Jesus Christ is the only lover worth looking for.
Now, my dear sisters, I will say a few words to those of you who have not yet given yourselves in marriage to the Lord Jesus.
This is a great sin. You are surely insulting the Lord who bought you.

It is also foolish of you to refuse and ignore his kind offers to make you Christ’s bride. By doing this, you throw away all the love he wants to give you. You choose rags instead of robes, trash instead of gold, pebbles instead of jewels, guilt instead of forgiveness, wounds instead of healing, dirt instead of cleansing, ugliness instead of beauty, trouble instead of peace, slavery instead of freedom, and serving the devil instead of serving Christ.
You choose shame instead of a crown, death instead of life, hell instead of heaven, and never-ending misery and torment instead of everlasting joy and glory.
Do you need any more proof of how foolish and mad you are to refuse and ignore Christ as your husband?
My dear sisters, I would take more time than you have if I tried to list every benefit you would gain by being married to the Lord Jesus.

This is your wisdom. Those who refuse are foolish virgins. But you are the wise virgins who have accepted the Lord Jesus Christ and given yourselves to him. You have made the wisest choice. The blind world may think you are fools. It may look down on you as “mad in a methodical way.” But God thinks you are wise. And one day even the people who now look down on you will see that you are wise.

It is your glory that you are married to the Lord Jesus. So be glad and proud of this marriage. But do not boast about yourselves. Boast in the Lord, who has given you these gifts so freely and kindly.

Being married to the Lord Jesus Christ keeps you safe. He will protect and defend you even from sin, from Satan, and from being lost forever. So far, then, you are safe. He cares for you when people put you in danger, and those dangerous times seem to be coming fast. Right now the danger is rising like a black cloud no bigger than a man’s hand. Soon it will spread over the whole sky, and when it is full it will burst. But if you are married to Christ, you are safe.
Now, my dear sisters, I will close with a heartfelt appeal to everyone—important and ordinary, rich and poor, all together—to be married to Christ.
Let me speak in a special way to you young women who are not yet married to Christ.
Maybe many of you came here just because you were curious. But perhaps this will be the time when you are brought home to hold on to the Lord Jesus and be married to him.
Oh, I hope that by his Spirit I can persuade you to give yourselves in marriage to the Lord of life!
If you are only brought to come to the Lord Jesus Christ and hold on to him, I will have reached my goal. Then both you and I will be glad that I preached this sermon to you.
Come, you young unmarried women, will you let me ask for your hand in marriage—not for myself, but in the name of the Lord?
Oh, I hope I can win your love and persuade you to give it to Christ!
May I be used to bring your souls to Christ!
May I be used to join you and Christ together today!

Do not be coy (bashful, shy; showing reluctance to make a definite commitment), as some of you may be in other love matters. Modesty and a young woman’s blush can look very fitting when other kinds of proposals are made to you. But here, being shy is silly, and holding back from accepting this offer is shameful. You have ten thousand times more reason to blush about refusing Christ as your beloved than about accepting him. Otherwise, the devil and sin will steal away your young hearts’ love.
No one has ever made you a better offer. No one has ever offered you a match like this one: to be joined in marriage to the Lord Jesus Christ.
Think about who the Lord Jesus is, the one you are invited to marry. He is the best husband. No one can compare with Jesus Christ.
Do you want someone who is great?
He has the highest honor there is. He is the glory of heaven, the darling of eternity. Angels admire him, devils fear him, and saints worship him.
Think of being married to such a great king! How much honor will that marriage bring you?
Do you want someone who is rich?
No one compares with Christ. Everything that fills the earth belongs to him.

If you are married to Christ, you will share in his riches, which no one can measure. Here you will receive from his fullness, one gift of grace after another. And later you will be welcomed into glory, and you will live with this Jesus forever and ever.
Do you want someone who is wise?
No one compares with Christ for wisdom.
His knowledge has no limit, and his wisdom matches it.
If you are married to Christ, he will guide you and give you advice. He will make you wise enough to be saved.
Do you want someone who is powerful? Someone who can protect you from your enemies, and from all the insults and put-downs of the Pharisees of our day?
No one is as powerful as Christ. The Lord Jesus Christ has all power.
Do you want someone who is good?
No one is like Christ in this. Others may have some goodness, but it is not perfect. Christ’s goodness is complete and perfect. He is full of goodness, and there is no evil in him at all.
Do you want someone who is beautiful?

His eyes sparkle more than any others. His loving looks and glances take your breath away. His smiles are the most delightful and refreshing thing for the soul. Christ is the loveliest person in the whole world.
Do you want someone who can love you?

No one can love you like Christ. My dear sisters, his love is too great to understand. His love is greater than every other love. The love of the Lord Jesus came first; it has no beginning. His love is free; nothing earned it. His love is huge; it cannot be measured. His love is steady; it never changes. And his love lasts forever.

My dear sisters, it was the love of the Lord Jesus Christ that brought him down from heaven. Love covered his divine nature with a human soul and body—for he is God over all, blessed forever. Love made him suffer hunger, thirst, and sadness. He was humbled all the way to death for you. For you who are married to him, he went through the painful, shameful, and disgraceful death of the cross. My sisters, can you hear this and not be moved when you think that the blessed Jesus went through all of this for sinful creatures like you and me?

Out of love he finished the work of rescuing us on earth, everything needed to make full payment for sin. Then his love carried him back to heaven, where he had been before. There he could apply to his people what he had bought for them. There he could pray for those he had rescued. And there he could prepare a place for them—glorious homes with himself, in the house not made with hands, which lasts forever in heaven.
It is out of love that he sends gifts like these from heaven to his people on earth. He brings them to his people by his Spirit, through the acts of worship he has commanded.

So surely no one deserves as much as the Lord Jesus Christ to be the one you marry. If you are married to Christ, he is yours—all that he is and all that he has. You will have his heart, and you will share in the best signs of his dearest love.
My dear sisters, the Lord Jesus Christ is begging you to be his bride.
We ministers have been sent by the Lord Jesus Christ to invite you to this very thing in his name. And Christ’s invitations are real, open to all, frequent, earnest, and free.
Christ’s invitation for you to be his bride is real. The marriage is real, and so, my dear sisters, you are really invited to it.

The Lord is not mocking you or pretending with you. Some fake lovers do that. They pretend to love young women until they win their hearts. Then they dishonestly and cruelly drop them, because they never really meant to get engaged or married. But the Lord really means it when he invites you. He has never thrown away anyone whose agreement and love he had won. Next,
My dear sisters, Christ’s invitations to you are open to all.

All of you are invited. None of you are left out. All kinds of sinners are invited. The worst and most disgusting sinners, the most famous lawbreakers, are invited to be Christ’s bride. They will be just as welcome as anyone else in the arms of his love.
Christ’s invitations to you are frequent. Jesus Christ calls you often. He has waited for you again and again, year after year. And today he is inviting you, through me, to come to him.
Do not brush off this invitation. Receive it with joy and thankfulness.
I beg you, come to this Jesus, who is inviting you like this to be his bride. Next,

Christ’s invitations to be his bride are earnest. He calls you—and not only calls, but calls with all his heart. Yes, he gives you many reasons. He will urge you to come to him. He does not want to take no for an answer. He knocks, and knocks hard, at the door of your hearts, asking to be let in. And surely you will not turn away the Lord of life and glory, who died for you and gave himself for you. Oh, my dear sisters, let this be the evening you are engaged to the Lord Jesus Christ!

He invites you to be his bride for free, because all his invitations are free. He does not expect you to bring money or property with you, as worldly lovers do. He wants nothing from you. In fact, you must come with nothing if you are to be married to the Lord Jesus Christ.

If you are poor, miserable, blind, and naked, Jesus Christ will make up for all of it out of his own free mercy. He will fill you and give you everything from his treasure house. He will make you fit for himself. He will prepare you to live with him forever.

Think about this: once you are married to Christ, once you are joined to him like this, you will never be separated from him. Neither people nor devils will be able to pull you apart. No one, no one, will separate you. Death breaks every other bond, but it will not break the marriage bond between you and Christ. Instead, death will bring you to have the one you love completely and forever.
So what do you say now, young women?

Will I get a “yes” to take back to my master? Or will I be sent away with a “no”? No, I cannot take a message like that to my master. I hope for better things from you, my sisters—things that go along with being saved. It seems to me that by now you should be starting to want Jesus Christ. You look as if you want him. You listen as if you are ready to say yes.
What do you say?
Will the match between Christ and your souls be made this evening?
Oh, I wish I could be the one who joins your hands together—or rather, your hearts! Oh, I wish I could be the one who ties the knot that can never be untied!

Some people marry in a hurry and are sorry for a long time afterward. But if you were once married to Jesus Christ, you would never be sorry. The only thing that would make you sad is that you did not join him sooner. And you would not be separated from him again for the whole world.
Will this be the day you are engaged to him?
Some of you have waited a long time. Will you wait any longer?

If you will not come now, you may never get another chance. This may be the last time you are asked, so it is dangerous to say no. Some of you are very young, too young for other engagements. But, my dear sisters, none of you are too young to be married to the Lord Jesus Christ. For other engagements you need your parents’ permission. But for this one, the decision is yours. You may give yourselves to Christ, and you should, whether your parents agree or not.
But some of you may ask, “What must we do to be married to Christ?”

You must feel your need to be married to him. Until you feel your need for the Lord Jesus Christ, you cannot be married to him. You must long for this Jesus and seek him, asking for a share in him. You must cry out to him every night to take you as his bride. Take off the filth of sin and everything that makes you dirty. And then, my sisters, put on the white clothes, the clean garments, that Christ has provided for you: the robes of his righteousness. In these clothes you will be beautiful. In these clothes you will be accepted. You must be wearing the wedding garment. You must take off all your own good works, because they will only keep you away from Christ. No, you must come without any goodness of your own that comes from keeping the law. You must have the righteousness of Christ.
So come to the Lord Jesus Christ, and he will give it to you. He will not send you away without it.

Take him on his own terms, and he is yours forever. Oh, give yourselves to him—soul, body, and everything—to be his forever. Then Christ will be yours. And then how happy, how happy you will be that you were ever born!

But if any of you die before you are married to the Lord Jesus Christ, then how terrible, how terrible for you that you were ever alive! But if you go to Christ, you will be married to the Lord Jesus. No matter how great your sins have been, the blood of Christ will make you clean from them. The marriage promise between Christ and your souls will wipe away all your sins. Then you will be tired of your old ways, because everything in your souls will become new.
Now, my dear sisters, I will finish by saying just a word or two to those of you who are already married to the Lord Jesus Christ.
Oh, be amazed, be amazed at the rich and free grace that has brought you into this relationship! Isn’t this the greatest example of love—that you should be the bride of the Lord Jesus Christ?
You had no beauty. You had no loveliness. You were full of sin. And yet he would embrace people like you and me! We would be taken into the arms of this Lord Jesus!
Oh, what endless kindness, stooping down so low!
Oh, what amazing love! I beg you, honor, honor this Lord Jesus Christ with deep respect.

He is your Lord. You must honor him, love him, and be faithful to him. Obey him, and be careful to please him in everything. Try to stay close to him in fellowship every day. Watch for Christ’s second coming, long for it, and get ready for it. Then the wedding between you will be celebrated, and you will live with him in homes of never-ending joy. There you will love and live with this King of glory forever and ever.

I do not know how to stop. I feel I could speak to you until midnight, if it would bring you to the Lord Jesus Christ and make you his bride. Truly, that marriage will bring you the greatest benefit, as you will find out for yourselves if you will only try it. And to help you do that, I will keep praying and keep working.

My dear sisters, I will spend everything I have, and spend myself too, for you. With God’s help I will keep going in this work I have started. Many of you may have time some evening during the week without taking time away from your work. So, my sisters, I will be either here or at a place that will be publicly announced. I will not care if people insult me or look down on me. The people of this world can call me whatever they like. They can say I am a Methodist.

In fact, my sisters, by God’s grace I have decided to use every method I can to pull you away from Satan, so that you may be like burning sticks snatched out of the fire. This will be my method. I hope it will be the way your precious souls, which will live forever, are truly saved.

If I am the one used to do this, I will be glad. Yes, I will be glad, no matter what people or devils say or do against it. May the Lord Jesus Christ guide me and help me at all times to do what brings him the most glory and what is best for your souls. And may you all say a heartfelt “Amen” to that.

“Now may the Lord Jesus Christ, who is God over all, blessed forever, help you and watch over you. May he keep you from all evil and sin here. And may he bring you before his Father without any fault on the great day when all must give account!

To this Lord Jesus Christ, the Father, and the blessed Spirit—three persons, yet only one eternal and invisible God—be all honor, power, glory, might, majesty, and rule, now, from now on, and forever. Amen, Amen.”

“May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. May they comfort you in trouble and rescue you from it. May they keep you safe as you go to your homes. And when you are there, may they keep you in awe of him, so that you live for his glory. Then to live will be Christ, and to die will be your eternal gain. And so may you live with him through all the ages and sing Hallelujahs to him forever. Amen.”
1 Corinthians 13:8 — “Charity never fails.”
Nothing is more valuable or more worthy of praise than charity. And yet no duty is practiced less.

We often pretend to feel concern and pity for the misery and trouble of other people. But we rarely feel for them enough to help them as much as we are able. Unless we give them what they need, for the body as well as for the soul, all our good wishes are just empty words. They are worth nothing and deserve no respect. When we hear that other people are in a terrible situation, whether they are friends or enemies, it is our duty as Christians to help them as much as we possibly can.

Of course, my brothers, we should not harm ourselves or our families. That is not the charity that St. Paul praises so highly. No, but if we are able in any way to help them without harming ourselves or our families, then it is our duty to do it. And this charity never fails when it comes from the right motive and has the right goal.

In the chapter before this one, St. Paul had been showing that there are different spiritual gifts. God gave one blessing to one person and another blessing to another. There were many different blessings, but God did not give them to one person. He gave one person a blessing that he did not give to another. And he gave the other person a blessing or gift that could make him just as outstanding in one way as the first person's gift made him in another. But although there are these different spiritual gifts, they are all given for a wise purpose, namely, for the good of all. That is why they are given out in these different ways.

On the one hand, we must not hide the gifts God has given us. On the other hand, we must not waste them on our lusts and pleasures, to satisfy our bodily desires. Instead, they are to be used for the glory of God and the good of souls that will live forever.

After Paul explained this in detail, he goes on to show that all gifts are worth nothing unless we have charity, however great they may be in themselves. You can see this especially if you read this chapter from the beginning.

But before I go on, I will tell you what the apostle means by charity. He means love. If there is true love, there will be charity. We will try hard to help and support others as far as God has blessed us with the means to do so. The apostle praises this very highly. So let us see how valuable this charity is, and how praiseworthy it is in all who practice it. I will do the following:
I. Look at this blessing as it relates to people's bodies.
II. Show how much more valuable it is when it relates to people's souls.
III. Show you when your charity is the right kind.
IV. Explain why this charity, or the grace of love, never fails.
V. End with an appeal to everyone, high and low, rich and poor, all together, to keep practicing this valuable and praiseworthy duty.
First, I will look at this duty as it relates to people's bodies. And,
1. Oh, if only the rich would think about how praiseworthy it is to help other people!

We were created to help each other. God has made no one so independent that he does not need help from someone else. The richest and most powerful man on earth needs the help and support of the people around him. He may be great today, but a thousand accidents could bring him low tomorrow. The man who is rolling in plenty today may be just as needy tomorrow.

If our rich men were more generous to their poor friends and neighbors, it would help win them the favor of others if God's providence ever turned against them. But sadly, our great men would much rather spend their money at the theater, at a ball, at a fancy gathering, or at a masked ball than help a poor, suffering servant of Jesus Christ.

They would rather spend their fortunes on their hawks and hounds, on their prostitutes, and on earthly, sensual, and devilish pleasures than comfort, feed, or help even one of their suffering fellow human beings.
When God demands their breath, what difference is there between the king on his throne and the beggar on the dunghill?
There is no difference in the grave, my brothers. And there will be none on the day of judgment.

You will not be excused because you had a large fortune and a fine house and lived with every pleasure the earth could give you. No, these things will be one of the reasons you are condemned. You will not be judged by how big your fortune is, but by how you have used it.

Right now you may think of nothing but your pleasures and delights, and of living in comfort and plenty. You never stop to think how many thousands of people would be glad to have what you are wasting and think nothing of.
I beg you, my rich brothers, think about the poor of the world. Think how good and praiseworthy it is to help those who are suffering.

Think how pleasing this is to God and how delightful it is to people. Think how many prayers will be said for your well-being by the people you help. Let this move you to give a little from the plenty God has blessed you with, to help his poor.

God could have put you in their low position and them in your high position. The only reason for this difference is that he was pleased to make it. Shouldn't this make you remember your fellow human beings who are suffering?

I beg you to think about which will serve you better on the day of judgment. Will it be the money you spent at horse races or cockfights, at plays or masked balls? Or will it be the money you gave to help your fellow human beings and the suffering members of Jesus Christ?

I beg you to think about how valuable and praiseworthy this duty is. Do not be angry with me for urging you like this. Jesus Christ himself and all his apostles praise this duty highly. I am speaking especially to you, my rich brothers. I plead with you to think about those who are poor in this world. Help them from time to time, whenever they need it.

Remember that a curse has been announced against the riches of those who do not use them to do good like this: “Listen, you rich people, weep and wail over the miseries that are coming on you. Your riches have rotted, your clothes are eaten by moths, your gold and silver have rusted. Their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have piled up your treasure for the last day.”

You see the terrible woe announced against everyone who hoards up plenty of the things of this life without helping those who are in need of them. And the apostle James goes on to speak against those who have gained their wealth by cheating, as too many have done in our day.
“Look! The wages of the workers who harvested your fields, which you held back by cheating, are crying out. And the cries of those who harvested have reached the ears of the Lord God of Sabaoth.
You have lived in pleasure on the earth and indulged yourselves. You have fattened your hearts as in the day of slaughter.”

So if you keep living for the desires of the flesh, pampering your stomachs and making them your god, while the poor all around you are starving, God will make these things a witness against you. They will be like a worm in your souls and will gnaw at your consciences forever. So let me once more urge you to show charity to people's bodies. I beg you to remember what the blessed Lord Jesus Christ has promised to those who love his members in this way: “as they have done it to the least of his members, they have done it to him.”

I am not speaking for myself now. I am not asking you to support my little flock in Georgia. If I were, you might say, as many recklessly do, that I wanted the money for myself. No, my brothers, I am now asking you to care for the poor of this land: your poor neighbors, your poor friends, yes, even your poor enemies. They are the ones I am speaking for now. When I see so many starving in the streets and almost naked, my heart is moved with pity and concern. It moves me to think that many people who have the power to lend a helping hand close their hearts to compassion. They will not help their fellow human beings, even though these people are in the most terrible condition because they have nothing.
I have urged the rich among you in particular to show charity. Now I want to,
2. Second, urge this on another group among us. Instead of being the first to do acts of charity, they are usually the slowest. I mean the clergy of this land.
Good God! How amazing it is to think that those whom God has called to work in spiritual things should be so slow in this duty. Bitter experience teaches us that this is so.

Our clergy (that is, most of them) are only looking for promotion. They run here and there to get one paid church position after another. They pile up wealth, either to spend on the pleasures of life or to satisfy their bodily desires. Meanwhile, the poor of their flock are forgotten. Worse than that, they are scorned, hated, and looked down on.

My brothers, I am not speaking about all the clergy. No, thank God, there are some among them who hate such behavior and are willing to help those in need. But God knows these are very few, while many do not give a thought to the poor among them.
They can visit the rich and the powerful, but they cannot stand to have the poor in their sight. They forget the poor members of Jesus Christ, and they forget them on purpose.

They have left the old paths and turned onto a new, refined road, but this road is not approved by the word of God. They have sunk into a fancy way of behaving. But however fancy it is, it was not the practice of the apostles or of Christians in any age of the church. They visited and helped the poor among them. But how rare this is among us! How seldom do we find charity in a clergyman!

It grieves me to say these things, but sad experience proves that they are true. If all the clergy of this land were here, I would tell them boldly that they have not kept to the ways of charity, but have neglected their duty. Instead of “selling everything and giving to the poor,” they will not sell anything, and they give nothing at all to the poor.
3. Third, I urge those of you who are poor to be charitable to one another.

You may not have money or the things of this life to give to one another. But you can still help each other by giving comfort. You can encourage each other not to lose heart, even when you are low in the world. Or when someone is sick, you can help as much as your time and strength allow. Do not be unkind to one another. Do not hurt, annoy, or get angry with each other. That gives the world an advantage over you.

And if God moves anyone to help you, do not misuse what his providence has given you through the hands of some Christian. Always be humble and wait on God. Do not grumble or complain if you see others being helped and you are not. Keep waiting on the Lord, and help one another from time to time, as much as you are able.
I have shown you how valuable this is for people's bodies. Now I go on,
Second, to show you how much more valuable this charity is when it reaches people's souls.
And isn't the soul more valuable than the body?
It would do us no good to gain the whole world if we lost our souls. In fact, it would do us infinite harm.
The soul is of infinite value and matters infinitely. So we should show charity whenever we see it is needed. We should also correct, warn, and encourage with all godliness and love.
My dear brothers, we should use every means and every opportunity to save our own souls and the souls of others.

We may have a lot of charity and concern for the bodies of other people and yet give no thought to their souls that will live forever. But oh, how sad it is to care for the part that dies but not for the part that never dies! How sad to show charity to people's bodies while we have no concern for their eternal souls! We may even help them toward their ruin, while we care nothing about their being saved.

You may love to spend a fun evening with them, or go to a play or a horse race with them. But you cannot stand the thought of going to a sermon or a religious meeting with them. No, you would sing drinking songs with them, but you will not sing hymns with them. To you, this is not refined enough. It is unfit for a gentleman of taste and unfashionable. It is only done by a bunch of fanatics and madmen.

So you are uncharitable enough to join hands with those who are rushing toward their own damnation. But you are not charitable enough to help bring them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God.

But this, my dear brothers, this is the greatest charity there can be: to save a soul from death. This does far more good than helping the body of another person. For even the most miserable person imaginable would be set free from all of it by death.
But for those who are not born again, death would be far from a release from all misery. It would be the doorway into all torment, and that forever.
So we should do everything we possibly can to keep a soul from falling into the hands of Satan. He is the great enemy of souls.
How this should stir you up to watch over your own souls and the souls of others!
For unless you are earnest with God, Satan will be too strong for you.
Surely it is the greatest charity to watch over one another's words and actions. Then we can warn each other when danger is near, or when the enemy of souls is coming.
If you have ever known the value of your own soul, and know what it is like to be snatched like a burning stick out of the fire, you will be eager for others to be rescued from that same condition.

Living a moral life, being honest, and paying everyone what you owe them do not prove that you are in a state of grace. They do not prove that you have been born again and made new in the spirit of your mind. No, you may die honest, fair, and charitable, and still not be saved.
The moral preaching that comes from most of our pulpits today is not enough to bring you from sin to God.

I saw that you were willing to learn, but you did not know that you must be born again. You did not know you must be made new, with all the old things gone and everything made new in your souls. My brothers, I could not bear to see you on the highway to destruction with no one to bring you back.

It was love for your souls and a desire to see Christ formed in you that brought me into the fields, the highways, and the hedges. I came there to preach Jesus to you, a crucified Jesus who died for you.
It was charity, yes, it was charity toward your souls, that has brought on me the harsh treatment I now receive from my brothers who are learned only in the letter.

So let me advise you to be charitable to one another's souls. Do this by urging them, with all love and tenderness, to follow Christ and the things that lead to their eternal peace, before those things are hidden from their eyes forever.
Now, in the third place, I will show when your charity is the right kind.
Here, my brothers, I will show first when it is not the right kind, and second when it is.
1. First, your charity is not the right kind when it comes from worldly motives or goals.

Perhaps you do it to be seen by people, or to get some advantage from them, or to be respected, or to gain a good reputation in the world. Or perhaps you are proud of it and expect God to reward you simply for doing it. If all or any of these is the goal of your charity, then it is all useless. Your charity does not come from the right motive. Instead, you are fooling your own souls.

If you give to the poor only so that people will notice, or because you expect God to favor you just because of it, then you do not care about God's glory or the good of other people. You care only about yourself. This, this is not charity. Nor,
Second, is it true charity when we give something to other people just to help them indulge in sin. This is so far from being charity that it is a sin against God and against our fellow human beings.
And yet it is as common as it is sinful to take our friends to one kind of entertainment or another, pretending it is charity, when all we want is to make them guilty of excess.
By doing this you are guilty of a double sin. We must not sin ourselves, and even less should we try to make someone else sin too. But,
Third, our charity comes from the right motive when it comes from love for God and is for the good of both the body and the soul of our fellow human beings.
When this is our only goal in helping suffering people, then our charity comes from the right motive, and we can expect to benefit from it. This is the charity that pleases God.
God is very pleased when everything we do comes from love: love for him and love for souls that live forever.

My dear brothers, think about this. It was love for souls that brought the blessed Jesus down from his Father's side. It was love that made him, who was equal in power and glory, come and take on our human nature. It was love that caused the Lord of life to die the painful, shameful, and cursed death of the cross.
It was love for souls that live forever that brought this blessed Jesus among us.
Oh, that this would help us see how great the value of souls was and still is! It was this that made Jesus bleed, gasp for breath, and die.
Surely souls must be of infinite worth, since they caused the Lamb of God to die such a shameful death.
Shouldn't this make you truly value souls?
The soul is worth more than anything. And this, this is the greatest charity, when it comes from love for God and love for souls.
This kind of charity will bring a satisfaction that lasts forever.
Oh, may this give you such a high regard for the value of souls that you will not miss any chance to do them good! Here is something truly worth showing charity to, because souls last forever.

So I earnestly beg you to think about the worth of souls that live forever, and to let your charity reach them too. Then, by your advice and warnings, you may be a tool in God's hands to bring souls to the Lord Jesus.
Next, fourth, I will consider why this charity, or grace of love, never fails.
It never fails because it comes from a God who never changes.
This does not mean that our charity is always the same. No, it can rise and fall like the tide, and it often does. But it never fails completely. No, the grace of love lasts forever.
There is, and there always will be, a charity toward everyone who has wandered and strayed away from God.
We cannot be at peace when we see souls on the highway to destruction unless we do everything we can to bring them back from sin and show them the terrible result of running into evil.
Christians cannot bear to see souls for whom Christ died perish because they lack knowledge. And if they see other people in bodily need, they will do everything in their power to help them.
Charity will never fail among those who truly love the Lord Jesus and know the value of souls. They will be charitable to those who are suffering.
So you see that true charity, if it comes from the right motive, never fails.
Now, my brothers, in the last place, I urge all of you, high and low, rich and poor, all together, to practice this valuable and praiseworthy duty of charity.

Riding around in your carriages, enjoying yourselves, and not thinking about the suffering of others is not praiseworthy. But helping your poor, suffering fellow human beings is valuable and praiseworthy wherever it is found.
But sadly, how very few of our fashionable, refined gentlemen think about their poor friends! Instead, they despise them and pay no attention to them.

They can indulge themselves in the foolish things of life. They would much rather spend their fortunes on lusts and pleasures, while the poor all around them are not considered worthy to be put with the dogs of their flock.

If you have plenty of the things of this world, you are welcomed as a companion by the refined and fashionable. But if you are poor, you must not expect any favor. Instead, you will be hated or considered unfit for company or conversation. And if you have plenty of the things of this life and do not need any help, then you have many people ready to help you.

My dear brothers, I have no doubt that your own experience proves what I am saying. It also proves that if anyone falls into trouble, those who promised to help completely forget their promise. They will even despise that person because Providence has frowned on him.

But this is not how people behave who are on their way to the heavenly Jerusalem. In this way our hearts and actions show that our lips are lying. For if we claim the name of Christ and do not turn away from all sin, we do not deserve to be considered real Christians.
For if we do not have charity, we are not Christians. Charity is the great duty of Christians. Where is our Christianity if we lack charity?
So I beg you to show charity to your fellow human beings who are suffering.

Truly, my dear brothers, this is really praiseworthy and really valuable. So I beg you, with hearts of tender mercy toward Christ, to think about his poor, suffering members. Practice, practice this charity, I beg you! If you have no compassion, you are not true disciples of the Lord Jesus Christ.
I humbly beg you to think about those who need help and truly have nothing, and to help them as much as you are able.

Remember, the kinder Providence has been to you, the more eager and earnest you should be to help those you find in trouble. What pleases your fellow human beings and doing your duty to God are matters of the greatest importance.

When you are called away from here, all riches and grandeur will be over. The grave makes no distinction. Great fortunes will mean nothing in the next world. If you have misused the talent God put into your hands, it will only make your condemnation worse on the great day of accounting. On that day God will come to demand your souls and to call you to account for how you used all the plenty of this life.
To conclude, let me beg each of you once more to act according to the circumstances of life that God has given you in his rich and free mercy.

Suppose you understood the great results that would come from acting in this charitable way, and saw it as a proof of your love for God, shown by loving his members. Then you could not have an uncharitable spirit. And you could not fail to help any of your fellow human beings who are suffering.

Think how easy it is for many of you to help someone in trouble by putting your small coins together. And who knows? The little you give may be what lifts someone out of trouble and into a thriving life. Then, if they have a truly Christian spirit, they can never thank God enough as the one who did it, and you as his instrument, for being such a good friend to them in their sad situation. Think also, once more, how much better your account will be on the day of judgment, and what peace of conscience you will enjoy.
How satisfying it must be to think that you have helped the widow and the orphan!
The Lord Jesus Christ recommends this, and it has been practiced in every age of the church. So, my brothers, be found doing this duty now.

I have spent more time on this because our enemies say we reject all moral actions. But, thank God, they speak against us without reason. We value moral actions highly. But we say that faith in Christ, the love of God, and being born again are worth infinitely more. Still, you cannot be true Christians unless you show charity to other people in trouble, whether they are friends or enemies.
So work hard at this duty, as the blessed Jesus has commanded. If you have true charity, you will live and reign with him forever.
Now to God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit be all honor, power, glory, might, majesty, and dominion, now and forever. Amen.
Genesis 3:15 — “I will make you and the woman enemies of each other. I will make your offspring and her offspring enemies too. Her offspring will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
As I read these words to you, I can speak to you the way the holy angels spoke to the shepherds who were watching their flocks at night: “Listen! I have wonderful news for you, news of great joy.”
That is because this is the very first promise of a Savior. God made it to Adam’s family, who had turned away from him.
We usually look for Christ only in the New Testament. But in one sense, Christianity is almost as old as creation itself.
It is amazing to see how God showed his Son to the human race step by step.
He started with the promise in our text. God’s chosen people lived by this promise until the time of Abraham.
To Abraham, God showed more of his eternal plan to rescue humanity.
After that, God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many different times and in many different ways. At last the Lord Jesus himself appeared in a human body. He came and lived among us.

Our first parents surely saw this first promise only dimly, compared with the great light we have now. Yet dim as it was, we can be sure they built their hope of eternal salvation on it. And by that faith they were saved.
How did they come to need this promise? And what does it mean, and how far does it reach? With God’s help, that is what I want us to think about now.
The fall of man is written too clearly for anyone to miss it. People who deny it actually prove it by denying it.

Even people who did not know God admitted it and were sad about it. They could see streams of corruption flowing through the whole human race. But they could not trace those streams back to where they began.
Before God revealed his Son, human beings were a puzzle to themselves.
In this one chapter, where our text comes from, Moses explains more than the whole human race could ever have figured out on its own. They could have studied forever and still not found it.

In the chapter before, Moses gave us a full account of how God spoke the world into being. He especially told how God formed man from the dust of the ground. God breathed the breath of life into him, and he became a living soul.
The three persons of the Trinity held a council about making this lovely creature.
The result of that council was: “Let us make man in our own image, so that he is like us.
So God created man in his own image. In the image of God he created him.”
Moses makes a point of repeating these words. He wants us to pay special attention to where we came from: our origin is from God.
No one has ever said so much in so few words. Only a man inspired by God could have done it.

But it is striking that Moses mentions our being made in God’s image only twice, and only briefly. It is as if he were saying, “Man was made with honor. God made him good and upright. ‘In the image of God he created them, male and female.’
But man fell so quickly, and became like the animals that die. In fact, he became like the devil himself. So it is hardly worth mentioning.”
We are not told how soon man fell after he was created. So if we try to set a time, we are claiming to know more than the Bible says.
Some people think man fell on the very same day he was made. I don’t think they have good enough reasons for that opinion.
The chapter before packs many events together. God made Adam’s wife. Adam gave names to the animals. God put him in the garden he had planted. I think all that took longer than one day.
But everyone agrees on this: “Man did not stand firm for long.”
How long or how short a time it was, I will not try to decide.
It matters more for us to ask how he came to fall from his firm position. We should also ask how the temptation that defeated him began and how it grew.
This chapter tells us about it in great detail. With God’s help, it will do us a lot of good to look at it closely.

“Now the serpent,” says the writer of this holy history, “was more crafty than any wild animal the Lord God had made. He said to the woman, ‘Really? Has God said you may not eat from every tree in the garden?’”

This was a real snake. But the one who was speaking was actually the devil. Perhaps that is why the devil is called “the old serpent.” He took over the serpent when he came to trick our first parents.
The devil was jealous of man’s happiness. Some think God made man to fill the place of the angels who had fallen.
God made man good and upright, with full power to stand firm if he chose to. So God was fair to allow him to be tempted.
If man fell, he would have no one to blame but himself.
But how could Satan make him fall?

He could not do it by force, so he tried to do it by trickery. He took over a serpent, which was more crafty than all the wild animals the Lord God had made. So people who are very clever but do not love God are just tools. The devil can use them any way he likes.
“And he said to the woman.”
This shows how crafty he was.
He spoke to the woman, the weaker one, while she was away from her husband. That made her easier to defeat. He asked, “Really? Has God said you may not eat from every tree in the garden?”
The devil must have said these words in response to something he saw or heard.

The woman was most likely standing near the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. (We will soon see her picking an apple from it.) Perhaps she was looking at it and wondering what was so special about that tree. Why were she and her husband forbidden to eat from it?

Satan saw this and wanted to draw her into a conversation. (If the devil can get us to talk with him instead of resisting him, he has already won a big step.) So he said, “Really? Has God said you may not eat from every tree in the garden?”
The first thing he tried to do was to get her to think harsh thoughts about God. This is how he usually deals with God’s children. “Really? Has God said you may not eat from every tree in the garden?
What! Did God plant a garden and put you in the middle of it just to tease you and confuse you?
Did he plant a garden and then forbid you to use any of its fruit at all?”
He could not have asked a trickier question to get what he wanted. Eve felt she had to answer and defend God’s goodness.
And so —
Verses 2 and 3.

The woman answered the serpent, “We are allowed to eat the fruit of the garden’s trees. But God told us about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden. He said, ‘Do not eat from it. Do not even touch it, or you will die.’”
The first part of her answer was good. “We are allowed to eat the fruit of the garden’s trees. God has not forbidden us to eat from every tree in the garden.

No, we may eat the fruit of the trees in the garden. (It seems this even included the tree of life, which was like a sacrament for man while he was still innocent.) There is only one tree, in the middle of the garden, that God has spoken about. He said, ‘Do not eat from it, and do not touch it, or you will die.’”
Here she begins to bend away from the truth. Sin begins to form in her heart.
By talking with the serpent, she has already taken in some of his poison. She should never have talked with him at all.
She could easily have guessed that no good being would ask her a question like that. No good being would try to plant such dishonoring thoughts about God in her mind.
So she should have run away from him. She should not have stayed to talk with him at all.
Right away the bad results show. She begins to soften God’s warning.
God had said, “On the day you eat from it, you will surely die.” Or, as it can also be put, “Dying, you will die.”
But Eve says, “Do not eat from it, and do not touch it, or you will die.”

We can be sure we are falling into temptation, and beginning to fall because of it, when we start to think God will not keep his word. That is, when we think he will not carry out the punishments he has warned will come on sin.
Satan knew this. So he cleverly
“said to the woman (verse 4), ‘You will not surely die.’” He said it in a sly, suggestive way: “You won’t really die.
Surely God will not be so cruel as to send you to hell just for eating an apple. That cannot be.”

How sad! How many people does Satan lead wherever he wants, like prisoners? He does it by flattering them that they will not really die. He tells them the pains of hell will not last forever. He tells them God is nothing but mercy. So, he says, God will not punish a few years of sin with misery that lasts forever.
But Eve found that God does exactly what he says. So will everyone who keeps on sinning with the false hope that they will not really die.
We can also understand the words as a flat statement, and that fits with what comes next. “You will not surely die. It is all a lie, just a scary story to keep you under control like slaves.”
For (verse 5) “God knows that on the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened. You will be like gods, knowing good and evil.”
What child of God can expect to escape being lied about, when God himself was slandered like this, even in paradise?
Eve’s mind must have been blinded to some degree. Otherwise she would not have let the tempter say such twisted things.
Look at the ugly colors God is painted in here!
“God knows that on the day you eat it, you will be like gods” (equal with God).
So the great temptation was this: from then on they would be under no one’s control. They would be equal to the God who made them, or even greater, knowing good and evil.
Eve could not tell what Satan meant by this. But she certainly understood it as some great privilege they would enjoy.
In the same way, Satan now shows sinners a path that seems right to them. But he does not tell them that the path ends in death.

To make this temptation stronger, Satan, or the serpent, probably picked an apple from the tree at that moment and ate it in front of Eve. That could lead Eve to think the serpent was smarter than the other animals, and could speak, mostly because he ate that fruit. So if the serpent had gained so much from it, she might expect to gain the same.
I think all this is clear. Otherwise, I do not see how it would make sense to say, “When the woman saw that it was good for food.”
How could she know it was good to eat unless she had seen the serpent eat it?
Now Satan begins to gain ground quickly.
Desire had taken root in Eve’s heart. Soon it would give birth to sin.
And when sin has formed, it gives birth to death.

Verse 6: “The woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes. She saw that it was a tree to be wanted for making a person wise. So she picked some fruit from it and ate. She gave some to her husband too, and he ate.”
Our senses are like harbors where our spiritual enemies come ashore.
That is why holy Job’s decision is so important: “I have made a solemn agreement with my eyes!”
When Eve began to stare at the forbidden fruit with her eyes, she soon began to long for it in her heart.

She saw that it was good for food and pleasing to look at. (Here was the desire of the body and the desire of the eyes.) But above all, she saw it was a tree to be wanted for making a person wise. She wanted to be wiser than God meant her to be. In fact, she wanted to be as wise as God himself. So she took its fruit, and gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate.
As soon as she had sinned herself, she became a tempter to her husband.
It is terrible when people who should help each other in the great work of being saved only push each other toward damnation. But that is how it is.
If we are good, we will stir others up to be good. If we do evil, we will lure others to do evil too.
What we do and what we teach others are closely connected.

So shouldn’t all of us be very careful not to sin in any way ourselves? Otherwise we may become the devil’s agents and trap even our closest and dearest family members. “She gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate.”
How sad! This one single act of sin was a tangle of many crimes!

They completely refused to believe God’s warning. They were extremely ungrateful to their Maker. He had just planted this garden and put them in it, and he had given them such a glorious, far-reaching grant of rights.
They also completely ignored their descendants. They knew their children would stand or fall with them.
Here was the worst kind of pride: they wanted to be equal with God.
Here was the greatest contempt for his warning and his law. They believed and obeyed the devil instead of God. And they did all this just to satisfy their bodily appetite.
No one on earth has ever committed a crime this tangled. Only the devil’s own turning away from God and his rebellion could match it.
So what were the results of their disobedience?
Were their eyes opened?
Yes, their eyes were opened. But how sad!
They were opened only to see that they were naked.
For we are told (verse 7) “that the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked.”
They were naked of God. They were stripped of everything holy and good. They had lost the image of God that they had before.
Now they could rightly be called Ichabod, because the glory of the Lord had left them.
Oh, how low these sons of the morning fell!
They fell out of God and into themselves. Once they shared in God’s nature. Now they had the nature of the devil and of animals.
No wonder they knew they were naked, not only in body but in soul.
And how did they act now that they were naked?
Did they run to God for forgiveness?
Did they ask God for a robe to cover their nakedness?

No. They were now dead toward God. They had become earthly, driven by their bodies, and devilish. So instead of asking God for mercy, “they sewed or wove fig leaves together and made themselves aprons,” or things to tie around their waists.

This is a vivid picture of every person who has not been born again. We see that we are naked. In some way we even admit it. But instead of looking up to God for help, we patch together a goodness of our own, just as our first parents wove fig leaves together. We hope that will cover our nakedness.
But our own goodness will not hold up under God’s strict judgment. It will do us no more good than the fig leaves did for Adam and Eve. In other words, it will do us no good at all.

For (verse 8) “They heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the trees of the garden in the cool part of the day. And Adam and his wife (in spite of their fig leaves) hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden.”
They heard the voice of the Lord God, or the Word of the Lord God. That is, the Lord Jesus Christ, who is “the Word who was with God, and the Word who was God.”
They heard him walking in the trees of the garden in the cool of the day.
Perhaps this was the time when Adam and Eve usually went, in a special way, to offer God an evening sacrifice of praise and thanks.
The cool of the day.
Maybe they sinned early in the morning or at noon. But God did not come to them right away. He waited until the cool of the day.
So if we want to correct others well, we should not do it when they are hot with anger. We should wait until the cool of the day.
But what a change we see here!
Before, they would have been glad to hear the voice of the one they loved. They would have met him with open arms and happy hearts. But now they hide among the trees of the garden.
How foolish this attempt was!
They must have been truly naked. Otherwise how could they think they could hide from God?
Where could they run from his presence?
But by their fall they had become enemies of God. Now they hated God their Maker and were afraid to talk with him.
Isn’t that our condition by nature too?

Yes, it certainly is. We work hard to cover our nakedness with the fig leaves of our own goodness. We hide from God as long as we can. We will not come to him. And we never would come, unless the Father came to us first, drew us, and gently pulled us to himself by his grace, just as he came to Adam first here.
Verse 9. “And the Lord God called to Adam and said to him, ‘Adam, where are you?’”
“The Lord God called to Adam.” (Otherwise Adam would never have called to the Lord God.) And he said, “Adam, where are you?
Why aren’t you coming to worship me as you usually do?”
Christians, remember this: the Lord keeps track when you fail to come to worship.
So whenever you are tempted to stay away, each of you should imagine that you hear the Lord calling you and saying, “O man, O woman, where are you?”
These words can be understood in another and better way: “Adam, where are you?”
What condition is your poor soul in?

This is the first thing the Lord asks a sinner and makes him realize, when God comes to him first and calls him by his grace in a way that truly works. He also calls him by name. Unless God speaks to us personally, and we know where we really stand, we will never value our rescue. We must see how poor, how miserable, how blind, and how naked we are. Only then will we value the redemption the dear Lord Jesus won for us by his death and his obedience.
“Adam, where are you?”
Verse 10. “He answered, ‘I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid.’”
See what cowards sin makes us!
If we had no sin, we would have no fear.
“Because I was naked. So I hid.”
Verse 11: “And he said, ‘Who told you that you were naked?
Have you eaten from the tree that I (your Maker and Lawgiver) commanded you not to eat from?’”
God knew very well that Adam was naked and had eaten the forbidden fruit. But God wanted to hear it from Adam’s own mouth.
In the same way, God knows everything we need before we ask. Yet he still insists that we ask for his grace and confess our sins.
For when we do this, we admit that we depend on God. We take the shame on ourselves. And in this way we give glory to his great name.
Verse 12. “The man said, ‘The woman you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.’”
Human nature has never been painted more clearly.
Look at the pride Adam picked up through the fall!
How unwilling he is to take the blame or the shame himself!
This answer is full of disrespect toward God, hostility toward his wife, and dishonesty about himself.
In it he quietly blames God.
“The woman you gave to be with me.”
It is as if he said, “If you had not given me that woman, I would not have eaten the forbidden fruit.”
People do the same thing when they sin. They blame their passions. Then they blame God and find fault with him for giving them those passions.
What they are saying is, “The desires you gave us fooled us. That is why we sinned against you.”
But God still punished Adam for listening to his wife. In the same way he will punish those who follow what their sinful desires tell them.
For God forces no one to sin.
Adam could have said no to his wife’s urging if he had wanted to.
In the same way, if we look up to God, we will find grace to help us when we need it.
The devil and our own hearts tempt us. But they cannot force us to give in unless our own wills agree.
So our damnation is our own fault. That will be plain to see on the great Judgment Day, no matter how boldly people talk back to God now.
Adam speaks disrespectfully about God, and he also speaks with hostility against his wife. “The woman,” or “this woman,” “she gave me.”
He puts all the blame on her and speaks of her with great contempt.
He does not say, “my wife” or “my dear wife.” He says, “this woman.”
Sin pulls apart even the closest hearts. It poisons holy friendship.
People who have been partners in sin here on earth will hate and condemn each other later, if they die without repenting.
All souls in hell accuse their brothers.
To some degree, it is like that even on this side of the grave.
“The woman you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
What a dishonest speech this was!
He uses fifteen words to excuse himself. But he uses only one or two words (in the original language) to admit his fault—if you can even call it admitting.
“The woman you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree”—that is fifteen words. “And I ate.”
How unwillingly these last words come out!
How quickly he rushes through them!
“And I ate.”
But that is how a proud heart that has not been made new behaves. It will put the blame on its dearest friend in the world, and even on God himself, rather than take the shame itself.
Because of the fall, we all have this pride. Until our hearts are broken and made truly sorry by the Spirit of our Lord Jesus Christ, we will always be foolishly blaming God.

“I have sinned against you, and you alone, so that you are shown to be right in what you say, and clear of blame when you are judged.” Only people who, like David, are willing to admit their faults and are truly sorry for their sins talk this way.

That was not true of Adam. His heart was not broken. So he blamed his disobedience on his wife and on God, not on himself. “The woman you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
Verse 13. “And the Lord God said, ‘What is this that you have done?’”
What amazing concern God shows in this pleading question!
“What a flood of misery you have brought on yourself, your husband, and all your descendants!
What is this that you have done?
You disobeyed your God, obeyed the devil, and ruined your husband—the one I made you to be a helper for!
What is this that you have done?”
Here God wanted to wake her up to see her crime and her danger. So he thunders in her ears, as it were. For the law must be preached to sinners who think they are good enough.
We must be careful not to heal sinners before we see that they are wounded. Otherwise we will say, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.
Sinners who feel safe must hear the thunder of Mount Sinai before we bring them to Mount Zion.
I fear that those who never preach the law are not skilled at bringing the good news of the gospel.
Every minister should be a Boanerges, a son of thunder. He should also be a Barnabas, a son of comfort.

Elijah experienced an earthquake and a whirlwind before the small, still voice came to him. In the same way, we must first show people that they are condemned. Then we must show them how they can be saved.
But wisdom is needed to know how and when to preach the law, and when to apply the promises of the gospel.
“And the Lord God said to the woman, ‘What is this that you have done?’”
“The woman said, ‘The serpent tricked me, and I ate.’”
She does not use as many words to excuse herself as her husband did. But her heart is just as proud as his.
“What is this that you have done?” God asks.
Here God accuses her of doing it.
She does not dare deny it or say, “I didn’t do it.” But she takes all the blame off herself and puts it on the serpent. “The serpent tricked me, and I ate.”

She does not say, “Lord, it was my fault for talking with the serpent. Lord, I was wrong not to hurry to my husband when the serpent asked me the first question. Lord, I plead guilty. I alone am to blame. Oh, please don’t let my poor husband suffer for my wickedness!”
If she had now truly repented, that is what her heart would have said.
But both of them were equally proud now. So neither would take the blame. “The serpent tricked me, and I ate.
The woman you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
I have described this part of their behavior in extra detail for a reason. It shows so clearly how great God’s free grace is. And it plainly shows us that salvation comes only from the Lord.

Let us take a quick look at the miserable situation our first parents were now in. They were dead, both in the eyes of the law and in their spirits. They were children under God’s anger, and hell was what they would inherit.
They had eaten the fruit God had commanded them not to eat. And when they stood on trial before God, they would not admit it, even though their crime was made up of so many wrongs.
What reason could anyone give for not sentencing these prisoners on trial to death?
Everyone must admit they deserve to die.
In fact, how could God possibly forgive them and still be just?
He had warned that on the day they ate the forbidden fruit they would “surely die.” If he did not carry out this warning, then the devil really could slander the Almighty.
And yet mercy cries out, “Spare these sinners! Spare the work of your own hands!”
So look! Wisdom comes up with a plan for how God can be just and still be merciful. He can keep his word about the punishment, punish the crime, and at the same time spare the one who did it.
Here an amazing scene of God’s love opens before our eyes. It had been hidden in God’s heart from all eternity!
Adam and Eve were still proud. They did not ask for forgiveness even once. Yet God immediately passed sentence on the serpent and revealed a Savior to them.

Verse 14. “And the Lord God said to the serpent, ‘Because you have done this, you are under a curse, more than all the cattle and every wild animal. You will go on your belly, and you will eat dust every day of your life.’” That is, the serpent would be kept under control, and his power would always be limited and held back.
The Psalmist says, “His enemies will lick the very dust.”
(Verse 15.) “I will make you and the woman enemies of each other. I will make your offspring and her offspring enemies too. Her offspring will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”

Before I explain this verse, I must point out a big mistake made by the author of The Whole Duty of Man. He claims that this verse contains a covenant between God and Adam. He treats it as if God were now making a personal agreement with Adam, as he did before the fall.

In his preface, where he talks about caring for the soul, he speaks about the second covenant. He says, “This second covenant was made with Adam, and with us in him, right after the fall. It is summed up in these words in Genesis 3:15, where God declares, ‘The offspring of the woman will break the serpent’s head.’ Like the first covenant, it was made up of some mercies to be given by God and some duties to be done by us.”
This is very false teaching. Those words were not spoken to Adam. They were spoken only to the serpent.
Adam and Eve stood there as criminals. God could not make an agreement with them, because they had broken his covenant.

And this is not at all a covenant in which “some mercies are to be given by God, and some duties to be done by us.” There is not one word here that points that way. It is only a declaration of the free gift of salvation through Jesus Christ our Lord.

From all eternity, God the Father and God the Son had made a covenant about saving God’s chosen people. In it God the Father promised that if the Son would offer his soul as a sacrifice for sin, he would see his offspring.
Now here this secret covenant is openly revealed. That is why God speaks so firmly and surely: “Her offspring will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
God had made an agreement with the first Adam before, and he proved unfaithful. So, to keep the second covenant from being broken, God put it into the hands of the second Adam, the Lord from heaven.

After the fall, Adam no longer stood as our representative. He and Eve were only private individuals, just as we are. All they could do was take hold, by faith, of the mercy God announced in this promise. They really did this, and that is how they were saved.
I am not saying that we don’t have to believe and obey if we are to be saved forever.

Faith and obedience are conditions, if all we mean is that they come before our salvation in order. But I deny that God offered these to Adam as terms. And I deny that God made a bargain with him in this promise, the way he did before the fall under the covenant of works.
How could that be? Adam and Eve were now prisoners on trial, with no strength to meet any conditions at all.
