Here is the truth. As a reward for Christ’s sufferings, God promised to give his chosen people faith and repentance, to bring them to eternal life. Both of these, and everything else they need for their eternal happiness, are made completely certain for them in this promise. Mr. Rastan, an excellent Scottish minister, shows this clearly in his book called “A View of the Covenant of Grace.”

This is not a needless distinction at all. It is very important. Because people did not know this, they have been led astray for a long time. They have been taught that they must do this and that, as if they were under a covenant of works. Then, they were told, they would be saved for doing it.

Instead, people should be taught that the Lord Jesus was the second Adam, and that the Father made a covenant with him for fallen humanity. They should be taught that they can do nothing on their own or for themselves now. So they should come to God and beg him to give them faith. By faith they will be able to take hold of Christ’s righteousness. Then they will show that faith by their works, out of love and thanks to the ever-blessed Jesus, their most glorious Redeemer, for what he has done for their souls.

This is a plan that holds together and agrees with Scripture. If we do not hold to it, we will fall into one of two bad extremes: Antinomianism on one side or Arminianism on the other. May the good Lord rescue us from both!

But let’s go on. By the offspring of the woman we should understand the Lord Jesus Christ. He is truly God from true God. Yet for us and for our salvation, the Holy Spirit would prepare a body for him. He would be born of a woman who had never been with a man. By his obedience and death he would pay for man’s sin and bring in a righteousness that lasts forever. He would give his people a new nature. In this way he would bruise the serpent’s head—that is, destroy the serpent’s power and control over them.
By the serpent’s offspring we should understand the devil and all his children. God allows them to tempt and test his children.
But praise God, the devil can reach no further than our heel.
There is no doubt that Adam and Eve understood this promise this way. It is clear that sacrifices were set up later in this chapter.
Where else could those skins have come from, which God made into clothes for them, except from animals killed as sacrifices?
In the next chapter we find Abel, and Cain too, offering sacrifices. And the apostle tells us that Abel did it by faith—no doubt faith in this promise.
And when Cain was born, Eve said, “I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Or, as Mr. Henry points out, it could be translated, “I have gotten a man—the Lord—the promised Messiah.”

Some go further and think Eve was the first believer. So they translate it like this: “The offspring (not of the woman, but) of this woman.” This makes the grace of God look even greater. The woman who was first to sin would be the first to share in redemption.

Adam believed too, and was saved. For the Lord God made clothes out of skins for Adam and his wife and dressed them. This was a remarkable picture of how they would be clothed with the righteousness of our Lord Jesus Christ.
This promise came true, word for word, in the person of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Satan bruised his heel when he tempted him for forty days in a row in the wilderness. He bruised his heel when he stirred up fierce persecution against him while he was preaching in public. He bruised his heel in a special way in the garden, when our Lord said his soul was so full of sorrow that he could die, and he sweated great drops of blood that fell on the ground. He bruised his heel when he put the idea into Judas’s heart to betray him. And he bruised him most of all when his agents nailed him to a cursed tree, and our Lord cried out, “My God, my God, why have you deserted me?”
Yet in all this, the blessed Jesus, the offspring of the woman, bruised Satan’s cursed head. Because he himself was tempted, he was able to help those who are tempted.
We are healed by the lashes he took.
He carried the punishment that gives us peace.
By dying he destroyed the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil.
By doing this he stripped the rulers and powers of their weapons. He put them on open display and triumphed over them on the cross.
This promise has come true in God’s chosen people, seen as one whole group, both before and after our Lord came in the flesh. For they can be called the offspring of the woman.
Don’t be surprised that all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus must suffer persecution.

In this promise, a hostility that lasts forever is set between the offspring of the woman and the offspring of the serpent. So those who are born of the flesh cannot help persecuting those who are born of the Spirit.

This hostility showed itself soon after the promise was given, when Cain bruised Abel’s heel. It went on in the church through all the ages before Christ came in the flesh. The history in the Bible and the eleventh chapter of Hebrews show this clearly.
It raged fiercely after our Lord went up into heaven. Just look at the book of Acts and the history of the first Christians.
It is raging now, and it will keep raging and showing itself, sometimes more and sometimes less, until the end of time.
But we must not let this discourage us. For in all of this, the offspring of the woman is more than a conqueror and bruises the serpent’s head.
That is how it was with the Israelites. The more they were oppressed, the more they grew in number.
It was the same with the apostles, and the same with the people who followed right after them.
That is why Tertullian compares the church of his day to a field that is mowed. The more often it is cut, the more it grows.
The blood of the martyrs has always been the seed of the church.
I have often sat down in wonder and delight and admired what God does. He takes the very plans his enemies made to stop his gospel and turns them into the best way of spreading it.

The devil has had so little success with persecution that I would think he would decide his strength was in sitting still. But I know that, according to this verse, he and his children cannot help persecuting.
What did he gain by persecuting the martyrs in the days of Queen Mary?
Wasn’t God’s grace greatly glorified in the way it held them up?
What did he gain by persecuting the good old Puritans?
Didn’t it lead to the settling of New England?
Or, to come closer to our own time, what has he gained by throwing us out of the synagogues?
Hasn’t God’s word been winning out powerfully ever since?
My dear hearers, please forgive me for saying so much about this point. God usually fills my soul when I come to this subject.
I can say what Luther said: “If it were not for persecution, I would not understand the Scriptures.”
Suppose Satan is allowed to bruise my heel even more, and his servants throw me into prison. I have no doubt that even that would only help to bruise his head more thoroughly.

I remember something the Lord Chancellor of that time said to the godly Bradford: “You have done more harm,” he said, “by urging people privately in prison than you did by preaching before you were put there.” Or he said words like that.
The promise in the text holds me up every day: “I will make your offspring and her offspring enemies. Her offspring will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
There is more. This promise also comes true not only in the church as a whole, but in each believer personally.

In every believer there are two seeds: the offspring of the woman and the offspring of the serpent. The flesh has desires that go against the Spirit, and the Spirit has desires that go against the flesh.

When grace makes a believer’s heart come alive, it is like what happened to Rebekah when she was pregnant with Esau and Jacob. She felt a struggle inside her and began to feel uneasy. “If this is how it is,” she said, “why is this happening to me?”

(Genesis 25:22) In the same way, grace and nature struggle (if I can put it like this) inside a believer’s heart, as if in a womb. But just as it was said there, “The older will serve the younger,” so it is here. In the end grace will win out over nature. The offspring of the woman will bruise the serpent’s head.

Many of you who have believed in Christ may find that some particular sinful tendency is still strong in you. It may be so strong that you are sometimes ready to cry out like David, “One day I will fall by Saul’s hand.”
But don’t be afraid. The promise in the text guarantees that believers will keep going and win the victory over sin, Satan, death, and hell.
So what if the sin living inside you is still there, and the offspring of the serpent bruises your heel by troubling and upsetting your righteous souls?
Don’t be afraid. Even though you are weary, keep pressing on. You will still bruise the serpent’s head.
Christ has died for you. And in just a little while he will send death to wipe out sin in you completely.

That brings me to the fullest way this promise will come true. It will happen at the final judgment. Then the Lord Jesus will present God’s chosen people to his Father without any spot or wrinkle or anything like that, glorified in both body and soul.
Then the offspring of the woman will strike the last, deadly blow by bruising the serpent’s head.
Then Satan, the accuser of the brothers, and all his cursed offspring will be thrown out. They will never again be allowed to trouble the offspring of the woman.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s kingdom. They will sit with Christ on thrones, in majesty, high above.
So let’s not get tired of doing good. For we will gather a harvest of comfort that lasts forever, if we don’t give up.
Dare, dare, my dear brothers in Christ, to follow the Captain of your salvation. He was made perfect through suffering.
The offspring of the woman will bruise the serpent’s head.
Don’t be afraid of people. Don’t get too discouraged about how deceitful your hearts are.
Don’t be afraid of demons. You will win the victory even over them.
The Lord Jesus has promised to make you more than conquerors over everything.
Plead with your Savior. Plead! Remind him of the promise in the text.
Wrestle, wrestle with God in prayer.
If you have been given the gift of believing, don’t be afraid if you are also given suffering.
Don’t let your enemies frighten you in any way. The King of the church has them all on a chain. Be kind to them and pray for them, but don’t be afraid of them.
The Lord will still bring his ark back, even though right now it has been driven out into the wilderness. And Satan will fall from heaven like lightning.
Is anyone here an enemy of God?
The promise in the text gives me courage to defy you. The offspring of the woman, the forever blessed Jesus, will bruise the serpent’s head.
What good is all your hatred?
You are just wild waves of the sea, foaming up your own shame.
Unless you repent, the blackest darkness is waiting for you forever.

The Lord Jesus sits in heaven. He rules over everything and makes all things work for the good of his children. He laughs at you with scorn. He mocks you completely, and so I will too. Who are you to persecute the children of the forever blessed God?
I am only a poor young man, but the Lord Jesus, the offspring of the woman, will give me the power to bruise your heads.
My brothers in Christ, I don’t believe I am speaking like this in my own strength, but in the strength of my Redeemer.
I know the one I have believed in. I am sure he will keep safe what I have handed over to him.
The one who promised is faithful. He promised that the offspring of the woman will bruise the serpent’s head.

May we all see this promise come true every day, both in the church and in our own hearts. May this go on until we come to the church of the firstborn, to the spirits of righteous people made perfect. There we will be in the presence of the great God, our heavenly Father, and truly enjoy him!
May all honor, power, might, majesty, and rule be given to him, together with the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and forever. Amen.
